title: Nue Kua: Repairing the Heavens
subtitle: A tradition transmitted through Werner's synthesis

learningObjectives.text: How does Nu Kua repair the sky?

repair.author: E. T. C. Werner (modern compiler and author)
repair.translator: not applicable; authored in English by E. T. C. Werner
repair.locator: Chapter III · Cosmogony-p'an Ku and the Creation Myth; Chapter III · Cosmogony-p'an Ku and the Creation Myth, normalized characters 8882-9269
repair.excerpt: The pillars of Heaven were broken and the corners of the earth gave way. Hereupon Nue Kua melted stones of the five colours to repair the heavens, and cut off the feet of the tortoise to set upright the four extremities of the earth. [7] Gathering the ashes of reeds she stopped the flooding waters, and thus rescued the land of Chi, Chi Chou [the early seat of the Chinese sovereignty].
repair.note: Quotation from E. T. C. Werner's 1922 English synthesis; it is not a direct translation of the ancient source it discusses.

narrativeBlocks.title: The sky cracks
narrativeBlocks.body: The rebel Kung Kung, defeated in a cosmic war, smashes his head against Mount Pu Chou — one of the pillars holding up the sky — and the heavens tilt, stars slip from place, and the earth tears open.

narrativeBlocks.title: The goddess who mends the world
narrativeBlocks.body: Nu Kua melts down stones of five colours and patches the broken sky; she cuts the legs off a giant turtle and plants them as new pillars at the world's four corners, and stuffs the flood with reed-ashes.

narrativeBlocks.title: A tilted sky that stayed tilted
narrativeBlocks.body: The repair was imperfect: ever since, the sky leans to the northwest — the myth explains why China's rivers flow southeast and the sun and moon roll that way across the sky.

narrativeBlocks.title: Our window is Ssu-ma Cheng
narrativeBlocks.body: This version reaches us through the Tang scholar Ssu-ma Cheng's commentary on the Grand Historian's records — a medieval scholar preserving a much older myth for us.

narrativeBlocks.title: A creator who fixes
narrativeBlocks.body: Nu Kua is the opposite of a distant maker: she is a repairer, a god who stays close to the world she shaped and mends it when it breaks.

quiz.prompt: What does Kung Kung's rage do?

choices.text: He smashes Mount Pu Chou — a sky-pillar — and the heavens tilt and crack
He steals the pillars of heaven

quiz.explanation: His headbutt cracks the sky — the damage Nu Kua must fix.

quiz.prompt: How does Nu Kua repair the heavens?

choices.text: She melts five-coloured stones to patch the sky and uses a giant turtle's legs as new pillars
She summons a dragon to hold it
She weaves a new sky from silk

quiz.explanation: Patched sky, turtle-leg pillars — and a permanent tilt left over.
